name: RX8111 Time Source
description: The RX8111 time platform reads UTC time from an Epson RX8111CE real-time clock (RTC) over [I²C](https://esphome.io/components/i2c/). Configure the I²C bus separately.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: Manually specify the I²C address of the RTC. Defaults to `0x32`.

config_entries.label: Alarm Day
config_entries.description: Match a day of the month (`1` to `31`). Cannot be combined with `alarm_weekday`.

config_entries.label: Alarm Enabled
config_entries.description: Enable the alarm interrupt. Defaults to `true` when at least one alarm matching field is set, and `false` otherwise. Set to `true` when only using runtime alarm actions; `on_alarm` requires the alarm to be enabled. Explicit `false` disables a battery-backed alarm interrupt without clearing AF; omitting this setting leaves a retained interrupt alone.

config_entries.label: Alarm Weekday
config_entries.description: Match a weekday (`1` = Sunday through `7` = Saturday). Cannot be combined with `alarm_day`.

config_entries.label: Battery Backup
config_entries.description: Enable the RX8111's automatic switchover to an externally connected backup supply at `VBAT`. Set to `false` to disable switchover and charging and run from `VDD` only. When omitted, the power-switch setting stored in the RTC is left unchanged.

config_entries.label: Battery Charging
config_entries.description: Enable the RX8111's backup charging switch. Requires an explicit `battery_backup` setting, and `true` requires `battery_backup: true`. Defaults to `false` when `battery_backup` is set; when both options are omitted, the stored charging setting is left unchanged. **Only enable this with a rechargeable backup supply and a charging circuit designed for that supply. Never enable it with a non-rechargeable coin cell.**

config_entries.label: Event Enabled
config_entries.description: Enable EVIN detection (`ETS`), its `/INT` interrupt (`EIE`) and the `on_event` callback. Explicit `false` clears only `EIE`, without clearing `EVF` or disabling retained capture.

config_entries.label: Event Level
config_entries.description: Detect `low` (default) or `high` voltage at EVIN. Requires `event_enabled: true` or an [RX8111 timestamp text sensor](https://esphome.io/components/text_sensor/rx8111/).

config_entries.label: Event Poll Interval
config_entries.description: How often to check alarm, timer and EVIN flags, timestamp records, and [binary status sensors](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/rx8111/), independently of the calendar `update_interval`. Minimum `500ms`; defaults to `1s`. Configuring a binary status sensor enables polling even when periodic calendar reads are disabled. EVIN event detection alone only enables polling when `on_event` or an [RX8111 timestamp text sensor](https://esphome.io/components/text_sensor/rx8111/) is configured; hardware event detection does not require polling.

config_entries.label: Evin Filter
config_entries.description: Hardware chattering filter: `0` (off, default), `1` (3.9 ms), `2` (15.6 ms), or `3` (125 ms). Requires `event_enabled: true` or a timestamp text sensor.

config_entries.label: Evin Pull
config_entries.description: `none` (default), `pullup_500k`, `pullup_1m`, `pullup_10m`, or `pulldown_500k`. Select a pull that holds EVIN inactive when external circuitry is not driving it. Requires `event_enabled: true` or a timestamp text sensor.

config_entries.label: Fout Frequency
config_entries.description: Set the `FOUT` pin to `32768hz`, `1024hz`, `1hz`, or `off` (high impedance). When omitted, the FOUT setting stored in the RTC is left unchanged. ESPHome does not measure this output; wire `FOUT` to the input that needs the clock. `1hz` stops while the RTC counter is stopped (see `rx8111.write_time` below). If the RTC routes the wake-up timer interrupt to `FOUT`, for example after other firmware set it up that way, the clock output is not enabled and the log shows `FOUT is routed to the wake-up timer (TMPIN); cannot configure clock output`; `off` still works. Starting the timer from this component, at boot or with `rx8111.start_timer`, moves the timer interrupt back to `/INT`, and a failed FOUT setting then gets a fresh set of attempts.

config_entries.label: Timer Clock
config_entries.description: Clock source: `4096hz`, `64hz`, `1hz` (default), or `1_60hz` (one tick per minute). The timer period is `timer_count` divided by the clock frequency.

config_entries.label: Timer Count
config_entries.description: Timer reload value from `1` to `16777215` (24 bits). Required when `timer_enabled: true` or `on_timer` is configured; also configure it to use `rx8111.start_timer`.

config_entries.label: Timer Enabled
config_entries.description: Enable the timer interrupt. Defaults to `true` when `timer_count` or `on_timer` is configured. An explicit `false` stops the battery-backed timer at startup; omitting the timer configuration leaves its stored settings alone.
